hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, APOE4 adheres more tightly to some recycling receptors than APOE3, impeding recycling.

scope: IN: binding strength or kinetics of apoE isoforms to recycling receptors (ApoER2/LRP8, LRP1, LDLR, VLDLR, heparan sulfate when tied to receptor recycling), pH-dependent dissociation in endosomes, and receptor surface levels/recycling impeded by apoE4 (e.g. ApoER2, glutamate receptors trapped in endosomes), including rescues (NHE6 inhibition) in apoE4 conditions. OUT: receptor-independent effects, binding to non-recycling partners, downstream synaptic function without a receptor-recycling readout.

row.Experimental system: Primary cortical neurons from E18 Slc9a6 wildtype mouse embryos, assayed at DIV10–14; no AD-model mutation reported. Cultures received human ApoE3 or ApoE4 secreted by transfected HEK293 cells at 5 μg/ml for 30 minutes, followed by Reelin at 2 μg/ml for another 30 minutes. Surface GluN2B was measured by surface biotinylation, NeutrAvidin isolation, and immunoblotting, with total receptor immunoblots. GluN2B surface availability is a readout of co-trafficked glutamate receptors, not a measurement of apoE binding to GluN2B; the neurons were mouse, not human.

proposed.why: Was 3/3. ApoE3 vs ApoE4 with Reelin read as surface GluN2B, a co-trafficked receptor rather than an apoE receptor, the same readout as reference P7.F5 (3/4).
